post-tgrx-linearized-horizon-model.physical_scope: An adopted first-order Einstein-Hilbert semiclassical model on a fixed smooth globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold with a stationary smooth null hypersurface, compact transverse cuts, an affinely normalized complete future generator flow, a supplied Hadamard state family and one fixed stress prescription. It asserts no null energy condition, entropy inequality, solution existence, physical accuracy, or general higher-curvature focusing result.

post-tgrx-linearized-horizon-model:
## Postulate

Use natural units $c=\hbar=k_B=1$, metric signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and the
curvature convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$ with
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=g^{ac}R_{abcd}$. Let $(M,g_0)$ be a smooth,
time-oriented, globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, and let
$H_0\subset M$ be a smooth embedded null hypersurface. Its smooth,
nowhere-zero, future null generator $k_0$ is affine, $\nabla_{k_0}k_0=0$,
with screen and expansion conventions as in the smooth null-screen definition.
Fix a nonempty compact smooth two-manifold $C$ and $\lambda_0\in\mathbb R$.
For each dimensionless $\epsilon$ in an open interval about $0$, supply a
smooth time-oriented globally hyperbolic Lorentzian metric $g_\epsilon$, a
smooth null hypersurface $H_\epsilon$, and a smooth map
$$\Phi_\epsilon:[\lambda_0,\infty)\times C\to H_\epsilon$$
such that $\partial_\lambda\Phi_\epsilon=k_\epsilon\circ\Phi_\epsilon$,
$k_\epsilon$ is future-directed and affine, and every
$\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}:C\to H_\epsilon$ is an embedding with spacelike
image. The family supplies a fixed identification of generator labels and a
fixed affine normalization across $\epsilon$. With $[\lambda]=L$, this
parameterization gives $[k_\epsilon]=1$ in length coordinates.

Write $q_{\epsilon,\lambda}:=\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}^*g_\epsilon$ for the
positive-definite induced metric on $C$, and let $\mu_{\epsilon,\lambda}$ be
its Riemannian area density. Call the reference geometry stationary in this
model when its screen deformation form $B_0$ vanishes along every generator;
then its expansion $\theta_0$ and shear $\sigma_0$ vanish by definition. Define
$\theta_\epsilon(\lambda,y)$ as the screen expansion along
$\Phi_\epsilon(\lambda,y)$ and
$\delta\theta:=\left.\partial_\epsilon\theta_\epsilon\right|_{0}$. Use
the stress tensor $T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}[g_\epsilon,\omega_\epsilon]$
supplied by the chosen Hadamard state family and one fixed local
renormalization prescription in the semiclassical model. No independent
graviton-fluctuation source is included in this perturbative family.
Select its Einstein-Hilbert submodel by setting the curvature-squared
couplings to zero, and define
$\delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y):=\left.\partial_\epsilon
(T^{\mathrm{ren},\epsilon}_{ab}k_\epsilon^ak_\epsilon^b)\right|_0$.
Here $G_N>0$ is Newton's constant with natural-unit dimension $L^2$;
$[\lambda]=L$, $[\delta T_{kk}]=L^{-4}$, $[\delta\theta]=L^{-1}$, and
$[\delta A]=L^2$.

Assume $\delta T_{kk}$ is continuous, its tail is absolutely integrable on
each generator, and
$$\int_C dA_0\int_{\lambda_0}^{\infty}(v-\lambda_0)|\delta T_{kk}(v,y)|\,dv<\infty,$$
where $dA_0:=\mu_{0,\lambda_0}$ is the reference background area density.
Adopt, only to first order in $\epsilon$, the linearized focusing equation and
future boundary condition
$$\partial_\lambda\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=-8\pi G_N\delta T_{kk}(\lambda,y),\qquad \lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=0.$$
Terms quadratic in expansion or shear are omitted only at this first
perturbative order: both vanish in the stationary reference geometry and are
of order $\epsilon$ in the supplied family, so their squares are of order
$\epsilon^2$.
This postulate is an adopted model equation; it neither asserts that the model
describes nature nor identifies its null-stress moment with modular energy or
entropy.

pthm-tgrx-linearized-area-modular-moment.physical_scope: A first-order geometric identity for a smooth compact cut of the stationary reference null hypersurface in the adopted Einstein-Hilbert model, with an affinely normalized future generator, fixed future boundary condition and absolutely integrable stress moment. The result has no sign conclusion and makes no entropy, modular-Hamiltonian, QNEC, QFC, generalized-second-law, or empirical claim.

pthm-tgrx-linearized-area-modular-moment:
## Statement

Use natural units $c=\hbar=k_B=1$, affine parameter units $[\lambda]=L$, and
the resulting dimensionless generator normalization $[k_\epsilon]=1$. Let
$C$ be a nonempty compact smooth
two-manifold, $\lambda_0\in\mathbb R$, and let
$\Phi_\epsilon:[\lambda_0,\infty)\times C\to H_\epsilon$ be a smooth family
of embeddings into smooth null hypersurfaces in time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifolds of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Assume
$\partial_\lambda\Phi_\epsilon=k_\epsilon\circ\Phi_\epsilon$ for smooth
future affine generators $k_\epsilon$, with a fixed generator identification
and affine normalization across the dimensionless perturbation parameter
$\epsilon$. Let
$q_{\epsilon,\lambda}:=\Phi_{\epsilon,\lambda}^*g_\epsilon$ be positive
definite, define the area density $\mu_{\epsilon,\lambda}$ by
$\sqrt{\det(q_{\epsilon,\lambda,AB})}|dy^1dy^2|$, and put
$A_\epsilon(\lambda):=\int_C\mu_{\epsilon,\lambda}$ and
$\delta A(\lambda):=\left.\partial_\epsilon A_\epsilon(\lambda)\right|_0$.
Assume the reference geometry $\epsilon=0$ has screen deformation form
$B_0=0$ along every generator, so its screen expansion and shear vanish. Let
$\delta\theta$ and $\delta T_{kk}$ be the first variations of expansion and
renormalized null stress in the adopted linearized future horizon focusing
model, satisfying
$$\partial_\lambda\delta\theta=-8\pi G_N\delta T_{kk},\qquad \lim_{\lambda\to\infty}\delta\theta(\lambda,y)=0.$$
Assume $\delta T_{kk}$ is continuous, integrable on each generator, and
$$\int_C dA_0\int_{\lambda_0}^{\infty}(v-\lambda_0)|\delta T_{kk}(v,y)|\,dv<\infty,$$
where $dA_0:=\mu_{0,\lambda_0}$ and $G_N>0$ has natural-unit dimension $L^2$.
Then the finite limit $\delta A_\infty:=\lim_{R\to\infty}\delta A(R)$ exists
and, for every $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$,
$$\delta A_\infty-\delta A(\lambda)=8\pi G_N\int_C dA_0\int_\lambda^{\infty}(v-\lambda)\delta T_{kk}(v,y)\,dv.$$
Consequently, if
$$M_\lambda:=\int_C dA_0\int_\lambda^{\infty}(v-\lambda)\delta T_{kk}(v,y)\,dv,$$
then
$$\frac{\delta A_\infty-\delta A(\lambda)}{4G_N}=2\pi M_\lambda.$$
Here $[\lambda]=L$, $[\delta T_{kk}]=L^{-4}$, $[\delta A]=L^2$, and
$M_\lambda$ is dimensionless. The quotient by $4G_N$ is only a geometric
normalization; it is not an entropy identification.

rem-tgrx-qnec-qfc-status.physical_scope: A source-scoped status distinction between selected quantum null energy inequalities and the quantum focusing conjecture. It establishes no entropy inequality, universal theorem, experimental result, or model applicability claim.

rem-tgrx-qnec-qfc-status:
## Statement

For a smooth codimension-two cut $\Sigma$ on a stationary null hypersurface,
one proved form of the quantum null energy condition (QNEC) bounds the null
stress $\langle T_{kk}\rangle:=\langle T_{ab}k^ak^b\rangle$ below by
$\hbar/(2\pi)$ times $S_{\mathrm{out}}''/\mathcal A$. Here
$S_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the von Neumann entropy of the state restricted to one
side of $\Sigma$, $S_{\mathrm{out}}''$ is its second variation under a null
deformation, and $\mathcal A$ is the infinitesimal transverse area used in the
source limit. The cited proof applies to its stated free or superrenormalizable
bosonic field theories on stationary null hypersurfaces; it is not an
unrestricted assertion for every state, geometry or dimension. The quantum
focusing conjecture (QFC) instead proposes that, for a specified generalized
entropy functional $S_{\mathrm{gen}}=S_{\mathrm{grav}}+S_{\mathrm{out}}$ on a
smooth null cut, its source-defined quantum expansion
$\Theta[V;y]=(4G/\sqrt h)\,\delta S_{\mathrm{gen}}/\delta V(y)$ cannot
increase under a further forward affine deformation $V(y)$ along the null
generators; $h$ is the determinant of the cut's induced transverse metric.
This remains a conjecture in general. Weakly curved
Einstein-Hilbert-Gauss-Bonnet models have QFC counterexamples in dimensions
$d\ge5$, and later tests prove a restricted QFC for a class of two-dimensional
Jackiw-Teitelboim toy models while also reporting QFC counterexamples in a
particular regime of that model. Those theory- and regime-specific results
supply no universal QFC theorem for arbitrary higher-curvature effective
gravity. The linearized horizon model on this page defines no outside entropy,
generalized entropy functional or entropy shape derivative, so it neither
assumes nor derives QNEC or QFC.
